raw_response:
I've been farming these 11.4 mu in Quzhou for 40 years, and at 64 I know every inch of this land. My household has six people and some of my family works off-farm, so I can't always count on labor at home — that means I keep things practical and stick with what I know works.

My main system is wheat-maize on 8 mu. For winter wheat, I always plant an improved variety — the extension station has been pushing Jimai types and they've done well for me. I'll rotary till before planting in early October, then put down compound fertilizer as basal dressing — that gives me about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, a bit more than the 15 kg the extension fellow recommends, because I'd rather spend a little extra than risk losing yield. I'll topdress with urea at jointing if the wheat looks yellow. I irrigate three times from my well: once before winter freeze-up, once at green-up in spring, and once at heading — pumping costs money, so three is my limit. I spray pesticide three times: herbicide early, insecticide once if I see aphids, and fungicide at heading. I expect about 480 kg per mu.

For summer maize, there's no time for tillage after wheat harvest in mid-June — everyone here direct-seeds into the wheat stubble. I buy hybrid seed every year because you can't save it. I apply about 16 kg nitrogen per mu, slightly less than wheat, and irrigate twice: at the big trumpet stage and during grain filling if the weather stays dry. Three pesticide sprays handle weeds and pests. I target 520 kg per mu.

I keep 3.4 mu for cotton because when prices are decent it pays better than grain. I plant hybrid Bt cotton in late April after rotary tilling. Cotton doesn't need as much nitrogen — about 12 kg per mu — but it needs more protection. I'll spray five times for bollworm and aphids. Two irrigations, at flowering and boll-setting, are enough. I expect around 260 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I don't change much from last year. The soil is the same, my well is reliable, and my family needs stable output more than experiments.
